target.title: Verify signed marketplace feed refresh
target.body:
## Summary

- Wire signed marketplace feed profiles into hosted catalog refresh using the signed envelope verifier and configured threshold.
- Persist bounded signed-feed trust state with hosted snapshots, and re-verify signed snapshots with the current source profile before using them.
- Count signed-feed thresholds over unique normalized Ed25519 public-key material so duplicate key IDs or duplicate key material cannot weaken a multi-signature threshold.
- Keep signed profiles fail-closed on invalid live bodies or unsigned old snapshots, without changing install eligibility or the existing marketplace refresh/entries payload shape.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/zod-schema.marketplaces.test.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.test.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxlint --deny-warnings src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.test.ts src/config/zod-schema.ts src/config/zod-schema.marketplaces.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.test.ts src/config/zod-schema.ts src/config/zod-schema.marketplaces.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `pnpm db:kysely:check`
- `git diff --check`
- `codex review --base fork/feeds-trust-source-profiles` - clean after verifier hardening

## Real behavior proof

Source harness from this branch generated an Ed25519 key, signed a hosted catalog feed envelope, loaded it through a signed feed profile, verified persisted snapshot trust state, then attempted offline fallback from an unsigned old snapshot under the same signed profile.

```json
{
  "acceptedSource": "hosted",
  "acceptedEntries": [
    "@openclaw/signed-proof"
  ],
  "acceptedTrust": {
    "mode": "signed",
    "signedBy": "proof-root",
    "signatureCount": 1,
    "threshold": 1,
    "verifiedAt": "2026-07-01T00:00:01.000Z"
  },
  "snapshotTrust": {
    "mode": "signed",
    "signedBy": "proof-root",
    "signatureCount": 1,
    "threshold": 1,
    "verifiedAt": "2026-07-01T00:00:01.000Z"
  },
  "unsignedSnapshotRejected": true,
  "unsignedSnapshotError": "hosted catalog feed offline mode; snapshot fallback failed: hosted catalog signed envelope is malformed"
}
```

Additional ClawSweeper fix proof:
The config schema rejects malformed raw base64url signing keys, duplicate signed-feed key IDs, and duplicate normalized public keys. The envelope verifier also counts threshold satisfaction over unique normalized public-key material, with regression coverage proving two key IDs backed by the same public key cannot satisfy `threshold: 2`.

## Stack notes

This is OpenClaw trust series PR #4 / OpenClaw PR #3, stacked after:

- #98299 signed hosted feed envelope verifier primitives
- #98316 source-profile trust config at `16cbe678ce`

The PR currently targets `main` as a draft because the dependency branches are on the fork. Reviewers should focus on the top commit `3ce0cfafaf` until the earlier trust PRs land.

target.title: fix(agents): cloud thinking models time out at 120s during reasoning (#80349) [AI-assisted]
target.body:
> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code.

Closes #80349

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running a cloud thinking model (e.g. `google/gemini-2.5-flash` with `thinking=medium`, the default thinking level) would see agent turns hang for ~125 seconds and then fail over with `FailoverError: LLM request timed out`, even though the provider was still streaming successfully. Google Cloud Console showed zero errors and p99 latency ~49s for the same `streamGenerateContent` calls — the response was being delivered, but OpenClaw's client-side watchdog aborted the run before the first token arrived.

The root cause is the embedded-run idle watchdog: `resolveLlmIdleTimeoutMs` applies a 120s network-silence guard for cloud providers. A thinking model legitimately emits zero stream chunks while it reasons server-side (often >120s for medium/high thinking), so the "silence means hung" heuristic fires a false-positive timeout. This is a regression-class gap — the watchdog already exempts local providers for exactly this reason, but cloud thinking models were not exempted.

## Why This Change Was Made

`thinkLevel` is now threaded from `runEmbeddedAttempt` into `resolveLlmIdleTimeoutMs` as `thinkingEnabled`. The implicit 120s network-silence ceiling is made thinking-aware: for thinking-enabled (non-`off`) cloud runs it is raised to the max safe timer value, so an explicit longer run/agent cap is no longer clamped back down to 120s; and when no explicit timeout applies at all, the implicit watchdog is disabled. Both mirror the existing local-provider opt-out and are guarded with `!isOllamaCloudModel` so Ollama `:cloud` models keep the cloud watchdog. Explicit provider (`models.providers.<id>.timeoutSeconds`), run, and agent timeouts are still resolved earlier in the function and still bound the run, so an operator who configures an explicit ceiling is never left without one.

The thinking-aware ceiling is applied before the implicit run/agent clamps (not only at the final fallback), so an operator who raised the hard cap to e.g. 300s for a thinking model gets 300s, not a re-clamped 120s false timeout. Scope is deliberately minimal: only the implicit cloud default changes for thinking-enabled runs. Non-thinking cloud runs, cron runs, local providers, and explicit-timeout behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on cloud thinking models (Gemini 2.5 Flash / Pro with `thinking=medium|high`, and other providers that reason server-side before emitting tokens) no longer get false `LLM request timed out` failures on the default configuration. Long-reasoning turns complete instead of falling over to the fallback model. Operators who want an explicit cap can still set `models.providers.<id>.timeoutSeconds` and it is honored as before.

## Evidence

Root cause confirmed on `main` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/llm-idle-timeout.ts`): the default-cloud branch returns `DEFAULT_LLM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000` with no awareness of `thinkLevel`.

Repro exercises the **real** `resolveLlmIdleTimeoutMs` + `streamWithIdleTimeout` production path with a stream that emits no chunks (a thinking model reasoning server-side), driven with fake timers past the 120s boundary.

### Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Cloud thinking models (Gemini 2.5 Flash, thinking=medium) abort at the 120s idle watchdog while still reasoning server-side, producing false `LLM request timed out` failures (#80349).
- Environment used for testing: Windows 11, Node v22.22.3, OpenClaw main @ 56d95b18f4, vitest fake-timer stream repro against the real `streamWithIdleTimeout` wrapper.
- Steps to reproduce: Resolve the embedded-run idle timeout for a thinking-enabled cloud run with no explicit provider/run/agent timeout, then drive a never-yielding stream (zero chunks while reasoning) past 120s and observe whether the watchdog aborts it.
- Observed result before fix: watchdog armed at 120000ms; stream rejected at 120s.
- Observed result after fix: watchdog disabled (0ms); stream stays pending past 240s.
- Evidence after fix (terminal capture):

BEFORE (unpatched main — 120s cloud watchdog fires on a silently-reasoning thinking stream):
```
[BEFORE] resolveLlmIdleTimeoutMs({ thinkingEnabled: true }) = 120000ms
[BEFORE] expected 0 (no silence watchdog for thinking); got 120000ms -> 120s watchdog ARMED (BUG)
[BEFORE] stream watchdog timeout = 120000ms
[BEFORE] after 120000ms of silence: stream status = rejected (reason: LLM idle timeout (120s): no response from model)
```

AFTER (this patch — watchdog disabled for thinking-enabled cloud runs):
```
[AFTER] resolveLlmIdleTimeoutMs({ thinkingEnabled: true }) = 0ms
[AFTER] expected 0 (no silence watchdog for thinking); got 0ms -> watchdog DISABLED (FIXED)
[AFTER] stream watchdog timeout = 0ms (0 = not installed)
[AFTER] after 240000ms of silence: stream status = pending
```

Real-source resolver verification (Linux, `ssh lxy-tx`, Node v22.22.0, tsx against the actual `resolveLlmIdleTimeoutMs` source — no fake timers — with the real Google endpoint reached for a `gemini-2.5-flash` thinking=on run):
```
[REAL] (main, BEFORE) resolveLlmIdleTimeoutMs({thinkingEnabled:true, model:gemini-2.5-flash}) = 120000ms
[REAL] (fix branch, AFTER) resolveLlmIdleTimeoutMs({thinkingEnabled:true, model:gemini-2.5-flash}) = 0ms
[REAL] Gemini generativelanguage.googleapis.com reached: HTTP 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (prepayment credits depleted on the available key) — endpoint + auth reached, but a full live thinking turn could not complete on the available quota.
```
The resolver value is the production function's real return: 120000ms on `main` (the false-timeout watchdog armed for a thinking cloud run) → 0ms on this branch (watchdog disabled). A completed live Gemini thinking turn would strengthen this further and is welcome from a maintainer with active Google quota.

Regression test: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/llm-idle-timeout.test.ts` — new cases assert (1) thinking-enabled disables the default cloud watchdog, (2) thinking-off keeps it, (3) explicit provider request timeout still honored when thinking is enabled, (4) explicit shorter run timeout still honored, (5) a 300s explicit run timeout is NOT clamped to 120s when thinking is enabled, (6) a 300s `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` is NOT clamped to 120s when thinking is enabled, (7) non-thinking still clamps a 300s run timeout to 120s, (8) local provider + thinking stays opted out, (9) Ollama `:cloud` models keep the cloud watchdog (and the 120s clamp) even when thinking is enabled. Full file: 87 passed.

Verification: `pnpm tsgo` pass; `oxlint` on changed files pass; `vitest agents-embedded-agent` `llm-idle-timeout.test.ts` 87 passed, `attempt-abort` + `assistant-failover` 28 passed. (`pnpm format:check` reports only pre-existing repo-wide drift; changed files are clean. `pnpm lint` shard `plugin-sdk boundary root shims` timed out locally — unrelated infrastructure timeout, not a finding on these files.)

### ClawSweeper review addressed

The first ClawSweeper pass flagged a [P2] timeout-ordering defect: the `thinkingEnabled` bypass sat after the run/agent timeout branches, so an explicit longer cap was still clamped to 120s. Fixed in the follow-up commit by making the implicit ceiling thinking-aware (applied before the clamps), and added the longer run/agent timeout regression cases above. The [P1] request for a redacted live Gemini embedded-run capture remains — that needs a maintainer with Google credentials (see "What was not tested"); the source-level repro above drives the real `streamWithIdleTimeout` path that fires the false timeout.

## What was not tested

- No live Google Gemini API call was made (no Google credentials in this environment). The repro drives the real production `streamWithIdleTimeout` watchdog path with a controllable stream + fake timers, which is the exact code path that fires the false timeout. A redacted live Google capture would strengthen this further and is welcome from a maintainer with credentials.
- macOS / Linux runtime not exercised locally (Windows host); the changed code is platform-independent.
- Full `pnpm test` suite not run locally (heavy); scoped embedded-agent shards run instead. CI runs the full suite.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I will resolve review threads I started or that point to addressed code issues.
- [x] Maintainer-judgment threads will be left open for human review.

## Compatibility / Migration

Backward compatible. No config, CLI, or public API change. The only behavior change: thinking-enabled cloud runs no longer hit the implicit 120s silence watchdog when no explicit timeout is configured. Operators who relied on the 120s cap for thinking runs can restore it explicitly via `models.providers.<id>.timeoutSeconds`.

## Failure Recovery

Revert the commit. No state migration involved.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: a genuinely hung thinking-model stream no longer aborts at 120s when no explicit timeout is set. Mitigation: this matches the existing local-provider behavior (same `return 0` opt-out for the same reason), and explicit provider/run/agent timeouts still bound the run. Operators wanting a cap set `models.providers.<id>.timeoutSeconds`.
- Risk: exempting too-broad a set of thinking levels. Mitigation: only non-`off` levels are exempted; `off` keeps the watchdog, and the `:cloud` guard is preserved.

target.title: test(ui-e2e): run Chromium capability probe headless with a timeout
target.body:
## Problem

`canRunPlaywrightChromium()` in `ui/src/test-helpers/control-ui-e2e.ts` gates the
ui-e2e suites by shelling out to `chrome.exe --version` synchronously (`spawnSync`),
and the helper runs at test-module load time.

On **Chrome for Testing 148 (Playwright `chromium-1223`) on Windows**, `chrome.exe
--version` does **not** print-and-exit — it launches a full **headed** browser that
never returns. Because the probe is synchronous, the entire `vitest` ui-e2e run
**deadlocks at the `RUN` header before any test executes**, and a visible "New Tab -
Google Chrome for Testing" window appears. Playwright revision **1208**'s `--version`
exits cleanly, so this is a CFT-148 regression on Windows.

The tests themselves are not the problem: driving `chromium.launch({ headless: true })`
with the matching binary directly is fully windowless. Only the capability probe hangs.

## Fix

Run the probe **headless with a hard timeout**:

- a clean `exit 0` still confirms the binary runs — unchanged fast path on Linux/CI,
  where `--version` exits immediately;
- a timeout falls back to the on-disk existence check (the binary is present;
  Playwright's own `chromium.launch()` surfaces any genuine launch failure) instead of
  blocking forever or popping a window.

## Verification

- **Before:** a `ui/src/ui/e2e/*.e2e.test.ts` spec on Windows (chromium-1223) hangs at
  `RUN`; a headed "Chrome for Testing" window is left open (reproduced standalone with
  `chrome.exe --version`).
- **After:** the spec runs to completion and stays **windowless** — 0 headed windows
  observed across the run, no lingering Chrome-for-Testing processes.
- No behavior change on Linux/CI, where `--version` already exits 0 immediately.

Based on `dd9706e90264e272ce7f155e00fa3cc83ee69b7a`; happy to rebase onto current `main`.

target.title: perf(slack): remove structural channel-side latency (serial prepare, global write cap, unbounded thread pagination)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101690.

Slack replies carry a constant ~1.5–2.5s of channel-side overhead compared to Telegram/Discord on the identical agent loop. The openclaw-rtt release canaries show Slack at ~3.1–3.5s p50 on every release since the Slack canary began (vs Telegram ~1.0s, Discord ~1.8s, same `mock-openai` provider), and a production gateway on 2026.6.11 with stock socket-mode config showed a 5.1s gap between `Inbound app_mention` receipt and agent dispatch.

Three structural causes in `extensions/slack`:

1. **Serial inbound prepare chain** — `prepareSlackMessage` awaited independent Slack Web API lookups strictly sequentially (assistant-thread metadata restore, sender-name resolution for allow-name matching, thread-starter lookup), stacking cold-cache round trips before the agent is dispatched.
2. **Process-wide write serialization** — the write client pinned `maxRequestConcurrency = 1`, so every `chat.postMessage`, `chat.update` (preview/draft edits), reaction, and file-upload call on a token ran single-file across the whole process, making unrelated channels queue behind each other.
3. **Unbounded thread-history pagination** — `resolveSlackThreadHistory` walked every 200-message page of a thread oldest→newest just to keep the last N, so the first message seeding a long thread paid one serial round trip per 200 thread messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `perf(slack): parallelize independent inbound prepare lookups` — starts the assistant-thread restore, sender-name lookup, and thread-starter lookup at the earliest point where their inputs and gating conditions are known, and awaits them where consumed. Drop/skip/authorization semantics are unchanged: every promise starts only after the gates that could drop the message, so dropped paths gain no new API traffic, and in-flight promises settle to result objects so an early throw cannot leave an unobserved rejection. Two further overlaps were deliberately **not** taken after code inspection: `authorizeSlackInboundMessage` does not unconditionally call `users.info` (channel/app_mention and open-DM paths can skip it, so an eager entry-time lookup would add API calls those paths avoid today), and `resolveSlackMessageContent` consumes the thread starter for inherited parent-file filtering (genuinely sequential).
- `perf(slack): drop process-wide write client concurrency cap` — removes `maxRequestConcurrency ??= 1` from `resolveSlackWriteClientOptions`. Provenance: the cap came from `107d2b7a096` ("preserve rapid send ordering"); that ordering contract is now owned by the per-target `KeyedAsyncQueue` in `send.ts` (keyed `accountId:tokenHash:recipient:threadTs`), which serializes sends per conversation without serializing the whole process. Slack's ~1 msg/sec limit is per channel, not per token. `@slack/web-api` (`dist/WebClient.js`) defaults `maxRequestConcurrency` to 100 via `p-queue` and pauses/resumes the queue on 429 `Retry-After` unless `rejectRateLimitedCalls` is set, so burst safety is retained at the SDK layer. Explicit caller overrides still pass through.
- `perf(slack): bound thread history pagination` — caps `conversations.replies` history fetches at 3 pages (600 messages). Threads that fit the window keep exact last-N behavior. Slack paginates replies oldest→newest with no reverse cursor, so for longer threads the fetch returns no history (logged) instead of silently attributing stale early-thread context — deterministic, documented degradation on a pathological path.

## User Impact

Slack replies dispatch to the agent sooner (fewer serial cold-cache round trips before the turn starts) and multi-part deliveries (preview edits, reactions, chunked posts, uploads) no longer queue behind unrelated channels' writes. Long-thread cold seeding can no longer stall dispatch behind an unbounded pagination walk.

## RTT measurement (openclaw-rtt `slack-canary`, mock-openai, 20 samples/side)

Both refs measured with the same harness, credentials, runner class, and sample count (dispatched via the openclaw-rtt channel-RTT workflow with an `openclaw_ref` input):

| Ref | Samples | RTT p50 | RTT p95 | Min | Max |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline `e591dcfa821` | 20/20 pass | 3,440ms | 4,802ms | 3,051ms | 4,812ms |
| fix `936f1855c4b` | 20/20 pass | 4,272ms | 4,928ms | 2,862ms | 5,527ms |

**Read this as a no-regression gate, not an improvement claim.** Both distributions are the same bimodal mixture (~3.3s and ~4.7s modes); the p50 difference is which mode samples landed in (8/20 vs 11/20 slow; Fisher p≈0.5) and within-mode medians differ by <60ms. Two harness properties cap what this scenario can resolve:

- The driver observes replies by polling (`1s sleep + conversations.history + conversations.replies` per cycle, ~1.4s effective cadence), which quantizes RTT into poll buckets — the source of the bimodality.
- The canary is a cold single-message channel mention: it never enters the thread-history, DM-history, allow-name-matching, or multi-part-delivery paths this PR changes.

### Where the canary's time actually goes (instrumented runs, 10 samples/side, per-sample SUT gateway logs + Slack server timestamps)

| Phase (p50) | baseline | fix |
|---|---:|---:|
| Slack event propagation to Socket Mode (server receipt → event arrival, zero OpenClaw code) | ~2,132ms | ~2,356ms |
| dispatch queue | 52ms | 50ms |
| agent turn (mock model) | 260ms | 249ms |
| outbound reply post | 240ms | 246ms |
| driver poll observation | ~820ms | ~890ms |

The dominant cost of Slack's RTT gap vs Telegram/Discord on this scenario is **Slack's own event delivery latency (~1.5–3.2s observed)**, which no gateway-side change can move. Total OpenClaw-controlled time (event arrival → reply posted) is under ~1s on both refs.

## Evidence

- Extension suite on Blacksmith Testbox: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack` — 106 files, 1476 tests, exit 0; `pnpm tsgo` exit 0.
- Repo-wide symbol sweep found no references to the removed cap outside `extensions/slack`.
- Autoreview: clean (one accepted finding during development — stale long-thread context — fixed by the no-history degradation above).
- Obsolete test asserting the removed default cap deleted; explicit-override test retained; capped-pagination path covered in `monitor/media.test.ts`.

Validation runs:

- `pnpm check:changed` lanes (remote-child) on Blacksmith Testbox: green (one initial `check:test-types` failure in the new capped-pagination test was a missing `as unknown` step in a mock cast; fixed to match the file's sibling pattern and re-verified green).
- 20-sample RTT A/B: openclaw-rtt workflow runs `28896305615` (baseline) and `28897212331` (fix); instrumented decomposition runs `28899719563` / `28899724145`.
- Branch-mode autoreview over `origin/main..HEAD`: clean, no actionable findings.

Follow-ups intentionally out of scope: the openclaw-rtt sampler's per-sample status probe still reads the pre-evidence-summary schema on its `main` (fixed on the measurement branch; separate PR to openclaw-rtt), and the canary driver's ~1.4s poll cadence limits RTT resolution.

target.title: feat: show live session activity for running tasks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

  Resolves a problem where the control UI could not reliably know which background work was active for a session, making it hard to show loading state, running task details, or polling-style progress for exec calls, subagents, and other session-scoped work.

  ## Why This Change Was Made

  This adds a live session activity surface over the existing gateway WebSocket protocol instead of introducing a separate REST endpoint, so the UI can subscribe to activity changes using the same session state channel.   Users can now see when a session has active background work, including exec/tool activity and task activity from subagents or related session work. The control UI can show a loading controller and running task list from the new session activity stream, while plugin authors get hook events for task and tool lifecycle changes.

target.title: fix(gateway): skip secrets.resolve when target SecretRefs use exec providers
target.body:
## Summary

reply-path `secrets.resolve` floods gateway log with `UNAVAILABLE` when model-provider secrets use exec SecretRefs but gateway credentials are plaintext.
- Problem: `resolveCommandSecretRefsViaGateway` skip logic only checks `ALL_GATEWAY_SECRET_INPUT_PATHS` (4 gateway credential paths), missing model-provider exec ref targets. Gateway cannot resolve exec refs, so every reply turn hits UNAVAILABLE → local fallback → log flood.
- Solution: Collect **active** exec target ref paths (not just discovered ones) and merge into the skip check alongside gateway credential exec refs. The target-exec collection is gated behind `resolutionPolicy.allowExecSecretRefs` and filtered to **active command targets only**, so inactive exec refs do not bypass gateway snapshot resolution for unrelated active targets.
- What changed: `src/cli/command-secret-gateway.ts` (new `collectActiveExecTargetRefPaths` helper with `activeConfiguredRefPaths` filter, `classifyConfiguredTargetRefs` now returns `activeConfiguredRefPaths`, skip condition extended, gated behind `resolutionPolicy.allowExecSecretRefs`) and `src/cli/command-secret-gateway.test.ts` (3 new/updated tests including mixed-target regression test).
- What did NOT change: Secret resolution logic, gateway protocol, config schema, default behavior for non-exec refs, `allowExecSecretRefs` policy handling.
- ClawSweeper P1/P2 addressed: `collectActiveExecTargetRefPaths` is gated by `resolutionPolicy.allowExecSecretRefs` and filtered to active command refs only — no-local-exec callers still attempt gateway, inactive exec refs do not poison skip decisions.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #96653
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a user configures model-provider secrets with `source: "exec"` (e.g. `models.providers.openai.apiKey = { source: "exec", provider: "vault", id: "openai/key" }`) while gateway credentials are plaintext, every `secrets.resolve` RPC during reply execution hits the gateway, which cannot resolve exec refs and returns `UNAVAILABLE`. The CLI then falls back to local resolution (which succeeds), but the UNAVAILABLE error floods the gateway log on every reply turn. This is pure noise: the skip logic already existed for the case where gateway credentials themselves use exec refs, but was scoped too narrowly and did not filter inactive exec refs.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Gateway log flooded with `secrets.resolve failed: UNAVAILABLE` when model-provider exec SecretRefs are present but gateway credentials are plaintext. Additionally, inactive exec refs in mixed target sets must not trigger the skip.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v22.11.0, branch `fix/secrets-resolve-exec-skip-96653`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
cd openclaw && pnpm build cliStartup
# Run dist bundle proof script covering 3 scenarios
node --experimental-require-module pr-96661-evidence/proof-v2.mjs
# Run unit tests including mixed-target regression test
pnpm test src/cli/command-secret-gateway.test.ts -- --run
```

**Evidence after fix**:

Live dist bundle proof (production built code, real exec child process) — 3 scenarios:

```console
========================================================================
  LIVE PROOF — PR #96661 (P1 fix: filter inactive exec refs)
========================================================================
Node: v22.11.0
Dist: dist/command-secret-gateway-C2q_A88T.js

[A] Active exec ref target → skip gateway RPC
------------------------------------------------------------
  Gateway skipped: ✅ YES
  Exec provider ran: ✅ YES
  Targets: {"talk.providers.acme-speech.apiKey":"resolved_local"}
  Diagnostic: talk reply: skipped gateway secrets.resolve because
    SecretRefs use exec providers at talk.providers.acme-speech.apiKey;
    rerun with --allow-exec to execute configured exec providers.

[B] Active env ref (no exec refs) → gateway called
------------------------------------------------------------
  Gateway skipped (should be NO): ✅ NO
  Gateway attempted: ✅ YES
  Targets: {"talk.providers.acme-speech.apiKey":"unresolved"}

[C] no-local-exec policy → gateway attempted (not skipped)
------------------------------------------------------------
  Gateway skipped: ✅ NO (correct)
  Gateway attempted: ✅ YES
  Targets: {"talk.providers.acme-speech.apiKey":"unresolved"}
  Diagnostics: doctor preview: skipped local exec SecretRef resolution...;
    doctor preview: gateway secrets.resolve unavailable...;
    attempted local command-secret resolution.

========================================================================
  SUMMARY
========================================================================
✅ ALL SCENARIOS PASS

  [A] Active exec ref → skip gateway → exec runs locally → NO UNAVAILABLE flood
  [B] Active env ref → gateway attempted (skip NOT triggered)
  [C] no-local-exec + active exec ref → gateway attempted (not skipped)
```

Unit tests (36/36) with real exec provider child processes + mixed-target regression test:

```console
$ pnpm test src/cli/command-secret-gateway.test.ts -- --run

 RUN  v4.1.8

 ✓ skips gateway resolution when gateway credentials would execute exec SecretRefs
 ✓ skips gateway resolution when target SecretRefs include exec providers
 ✓ skips local exec SecretRef fallback when the caller disallows exec providers
 ✓ does not skip gateway resolution when only inactive targets use exec SecretRefs (NEW)
 ✓ keeps local exec SecretRef fallback enabled by default
 ...
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  36 passed (36)
```

Key tests and what they prove:

| Test | What it proves |
|------|---------------|
| `skips gateway resolution when gateway credentials would execute exec SecretRefs` | Gateway-credential exec ref path still works (regression) |
| `skips gateway resolution when target SecretRefs include exec providers` | Target exec ref skip works; gateway creds are plaintext, `callGateway` not called |
| `skips local exec SecretRef fallback when the caller disallows exec providers` | ClawSweeper P1 gate: with `allowLocalExecSecretRefs: false`, gateway is attempted (not skipped); exec ref stays unresolved |
| `does not skip gateway resolution when only inactive targets use exec SecretRefs` | **NEW** — ClawSweeper P1 refinement: inactive exec ref does not trigger gateway skip; active env ref still goes through gateway |
| `keeps local exec SecretRef fallback enabled by default` | Existing gateway UNAVAILABLE path still works (regression) |

**Observed result after fix**:
- Gateway `secrets.resolve` RPC is not attempted when any **active** target SecretRef uses an exec provider
- Inactive exec refs no longer poison the skip decision — mixed target sets still go through gateway snapshot resolution
- `allowLocalExecSecretRefs=false` callers (e.g. doctor preview) still attempt the gateway (not skipped)
- Diagnostic message unified: `skipped gateway secrets.resolve because SecretRefs use exec providers at ...`
- Reply and command paths benefit equally (the skip is in `resolveCommandSecretRefsViaGateway`, shared by all callers)

**What was not tested**:
- Non-talk provider targets (e.g. web search, channel credentials) — the same shared `resolveCommandSecretRefsViaGateway` applies; target discovery is generic
- Live gateway round-trip with real mixed targets (no local gateway available) — covered by unit test with mocked gateway snapshot

## Root Cause (if applicable)

Introduced by commit `1ee2733b2f` (Vincent Koc, 2026-06-17, `fix(qa-lab): harden live cleanup and readiness`). The `collectActiveGatewayExecSecretRefCredentialPaths` function filters `ALL_GATEWAY_SECRET_INPUT_PATHS` — only 4 gateway credential paths (`gateway.auth.token/password`, `gateway.remote.token/password`). Model-provider secrets (`models.providers.*.apiKey`, etc.) are never checked. The target ref paths were already known at the decision point, but this information was discarded before the skip check.

Additionally, ClawSweeper review identified: `collectActiveExecTargetRefPaths` collected **all** discovered exec refs including inactive ones, which could bypass gateway snapshot resolution for unrelated active targets in mixed target sets.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Target test: `src/cli/command-secret-gateway.test.ts`
- Existing test "skips gateway resolution when gateway credentials would execute exec SecretRefs" — verifies gateway-credential exec ref path still works
- New test "skips gateway resolution when target SecretRefs include exec providers" — verifies active target exec ref triggers skip
- New test "does not skip gateway resolution when only inactive targets use exec SecretRefs" — verifies inactive exec ref does not trigger skip

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None. The fix changes when the skip triggers (earlier in more cases for active exec refs, not at all for inactive exec refs) but the resolution outcome is identical — local resolution was already the fallback after UNAVAILABLE. Users with model-provider exec refs will see fewer `UNAVAILABLE` warnings in the gateway log. Users with only inactive exec refs see no behavior change.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No — same local resolution code path
- [x] New/changed network calls? No — fewer gateway RPCs
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Source-code trace of skip condition logic, 3-scenario live dist bundle proof, unit test scenario walkthrough
- Edge cases checked: Gateway creds exec + target exec (merged diagnostic), gateway creds plaintext + target exec (new fix path), gateway creds exec + target plaintext (existing behavior preserved), active env ref + inactive exec ref (P1 fix — gateway called), no-local-exec policy (P1 gate — not skipped)
- What you did NOT verify: Non-talk provider targets (shared resolver covers all; `activeConfiguredRefPaths` is computed from `classifyConfiguredTargetRefs` which is target-agnostic); live gateway with real mixed exec targets

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — existing users with active exec refs get fewer log lines; users with inactive exec refs see no change
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The skip condition is the correct boundary — if any **active** target uses exec ref, gateway cannot resolve it, so skip unconditionally. Inactive exec refs are correctly excluded using the pre-existing active/inactive classification from `classifyConfiguredTargetRefs`.
- **Refactor needed**: No. The new helper `collectActiveExecTargetRefPaths` follows the same pattern as existing helpers. `classifyConfiguredTargetRefs` returns an additional field (`activeConfiguredRefPaths`) that is a natural byproduct of its existing computation.
- **Alternative considered**: Extending `ALL_GATEWAY_SECRET_INPUT_PATHS` to include model-provider paths — rejected because those are not fixed paths (different providers have different key paths), making a static list fragile and incomplete. Collecting all discovered exec refs unconditionally — rejected because inactive exec refs in mixed target sets would bypass gateway snapshot resolution for active non-exec targets.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue #96653 analysis → root-cause trace → fix design → implementation → ClawSweeper P1 refinement (filter inactive exec refs) → pre-commit review → live proof

## Risks and Mitigations

None. The fix only expands when the gateway RPC skip triggers. The local fallback path is the same code that already executed after every UNAVAILABLE error. The active/inactive filter reuses the pre-existing classification from `classifyConfiguredTargetRefs`. Three merge-risk labels are addressed:
- `🚨 auth-provider` — inactive exec refs do not affect active model-provider credential resolution
- `🚨 compatibility` — users with only inactive exec refs see no behavior change
- `🚨 security-boundary` — only active exec refs enter local resolution path; inactive exec refs do not change security boundaries

No new code path is introduced for resolution, only for the skip decision. All existing tests continue to pass (36/36, including new mixed-target regression test).

target.title: fix(mattermost): key private channels as group on outbound routing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves #95646.

The `chat_type` OpenClaw uses for a Mattermost **private channel** is non-deterministic across code paths:

- **Inbound** classifies by channel *type* — `P`/`G` → `group` (authoritative, correct).
- **Outbound / session reconstruction** re-derives it from the delivery *target string* `channel:<id>` (a private channel is addressed with the *same prefix* as a public channel) → `channel`.

So one private-channel conversation is keyed under two session namespaces — `…:mattermost:group:<id>:thread:<root>` (inbound) and a phantom `…:channel:<id>:thread:<root>` (delivery). Threaded/scheduled deliveries (e.g. a recheck cron) then split the thread across namespaces, and on a cold restart the delivery rebuilds as `channel:` and thread recovery fails.

Root cause: nothing on the outbound path could represent `group`, and the **isolated cron delivery path** resolved the route from the ephemeral run key rather than the job's bound conversation identity.

## Fix

Three coordinated changes, all sourcing the authoritative type **without a channel-type cache**:

1. **`extensions/mattermost/src/session-route.ts`** — `resolveMattermostOutboundSessionRoute` keys a conversation as `group` from an authoritative signal: the resolved target kind, an explicit `group:` prefix, or the inbound `currentSessionKey`'s peer kind.
2. **`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/target-resolution.ts`** — `resolveMattermostOpaqueTarget` classifies a bare channel id by its real channel type (`P`/`G` → group), cached per id.
3. **`src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts`** — isolated cron deliveries now resolve the outbound route from the job's **bound** conversation session key (when it is a real conversation key), not the isolated run key, so the namespace survives (new `selectCronRouteCurrentSessionKey` helper). This is the path that was forking the phantom `channel:` session.

The **wire target stays `channel:<id>`** for non-DMs — Mattermost posts to the channel id regardless, and `parseMattermostTarget` only accepts `channel:`/`user:`. The `group` distinction lives in the session key (`peer.kind`), which is the namespace that was mismatching.

## Scope & why this design

This targets the routing/session half of the Mattermost `group` overload (the prompt-intro half landed separately in #96244). It deliberately uses **`currentSessionKey` identity, not a channel-kind cache**: a sibling PR (#96521) that added a 30‑minute channel-kind cache documented two correctness issues with that approach — a **cold-restart regression** (empty cache rebuilds `channel:` routes and thread recovery fails) and a **cache-TTL mismatch** vs the 5‑minute authoritative lookup. Keying off the bound session identity avoids both: it is correct cold, with no extra cache.

## What changed

- `extensions/mattermost/src/session-route.ts` (+ test) — honor a `group` signal; never declare a `chat_type` from the lossy prefix.
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/target-resolution.ts` (+ test) — classify `P`/`G` channels as `group` via channel-type lookup (cached).
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts` (+ test) — prefer the job's bound conversation key for cron delivery route resolution.

## Public-channel regression fix (review follow-up)

Review flagged that selecting the `group` namespace from `resolvedTarget.kind === "group"` could also catch a **public** `O` channel, because `listMattermostDirectoryGroups` labeled *every* joined channel (public `O` **and** private `P`) as kind `group`. A name-resolved public channel would then fork a phantom `group:<id>` session — the mirror image of the original bug.

Fixed at the source: the directory listing now derives each entry's kind from the **authoritative Mattermost channel type** (`mapMattermostChannelTypeToChatType`: `O` -> `channel`, `P`/`G` -> `group`), so a public channel never presents as `group` to the outbound route. The route's group selection is unchanged because its `resolvedKind === "group"` signal is now always authoritative. Added a regression test: a public `O` channel resolves to kind `channel`, a private `P` channel to `group`.

- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/directory.ts` — authoritative per-channel kind for directory entries.
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/directory.test.ts` — public `O` -> `channel`, private `P` -> `group` regression coverage.

## Evidence

**Unit tests (added):** session-route group keying (resolved-kind / `group:` prefix / inbound `currentSessionKey`), resolver `P`→group, and `selectCronRouteCurrentSessionKey` (bound conversation key preferred, isolated/cron keys ignored). All green; `tsgo`/`check:test-types` clean.

**Live Mattermost proof (deployed build, private channel type `P`, redacted ids):** a scheduled **announce** delivery into a private-channel thread, observing the session store before/after:

| build | thread | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| **without the cron fix** | `…mofm…` | `group:<id>:thread` only | a phantom `channel:<id>:thread` is **created** (the #95646 split) |
| **with the cron fix** | `…5x48…` | `group:<id>:thread` only | **no `channel:` session** — the delivery reuses `group:<id>:thread` |

In both cases the message was delivered into the thread (root matched). With the fix the outbound delivery **reuses the inbound `group:<id>` namespace** instead of forking `channel:<id>`. The same split is observable in untouched production data: existing private-channel threads carry both `group:<id>:thread:<root>` and a phantom `channel:<id>:thread:<root>` for the same root.

**Visual (deployed build, private channel, redacted):** the scheduled `PROOF_96645_PATCHED_OK` reply lands *inside* the thread, and the agent confirms the inbound `chat_type` for this channel is `group`:

![private-channel thread delivery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iloveleon19/openclaw/pr-proof-assets/proof-96645-thread.png)

target.title: fix(ollama): remote Ollama streaming stalls at model_call:started on slow hosts
target.body:
Closes #94251

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running a remote Ollama provider (Ollama on a different machine than OpenClaw, especially slow CPU-only inference) would never receive a chat response. The session stalls indefinitely at `model_call:started`, and the remote Ollama host shows the model going to `Stopping...` mid-generation — the server sees the client disconnect. Direct `curl` from the same host streams fine, so the failure is specific to OpenClaw's native Ollama stream client.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native Ollama stream path (`createRawOllamaStreamFn`) requests a stream through `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, which arms an `AbortController`-based deadline (`buildTimeoutAbortSignal`) and returns a `refreshTimeout` callback. That callback is the documented contract for converting the deadline into a no-progress (idle) timeout: it must be called as the body is consumed. The OpenAI-compatible transport (`src/agents/provider-transport-fetch.ts`) and MCP HTTP fetch (`src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.ts`) both call `refreshTimeout()` on every chunk. The Ollama native path destructured only `{ response, release }` and never called it, so the configured request timeout acted as a hard wall-clock cap. Once a configured `timeoutSeconds` elapsed while a slow remote model was still streaming, the request was aborted mid-stream, the server saw a disconnect, and the run stalled. The fix calls `refreshTimeout?.()` for each consumed NDJSON chunk, matching the existing sibling contract.

## User Impact

Remote/slow Ollama hosts now stream to completion: the request deadline behaves as a no-progress timeout (reset on every chunk) rather than a total wall-clock cap. Chat sessions backed by a remote Ollama model return responses instead of hanging at `model_call:started`. No config or API changes.

## Evidence

Added a regression test asserting `refreshTimeout` is called once per streamed NDJSON chunk.

Before the production fix (test reverted), the test fails:

```
× refreshes the guarded-fetch idle timeout for each streamed chunk
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called 3 times, but got 0 times
 ❯ extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts:491:28
   491| expect(refreshTimeout).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(chunks.length);
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 15 passed (16)
```

After the fix:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
```

Also green on the touched area: `tsgo` extensions typecheck (exit 0), oxlint (exit 0), oxfmt --check (all files correctly formatted).

target.title: feat(whatsapp): add throttled progress messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp cannot edit already-sent messages, so long-running turns can look idle even when lifecycle status reactions are enabled. Users who ask for work that takes more than a short moment, such as tool calls, searches, command execution, or code edits, need a low-noise way to see that OpenClaw is still working.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an opt-in `channels.whatsapp.progressMessages` config surface for sparse text progress messages during long WhatsApp turns. The runtime waits for the configured initial delay, throttles additional progress messages, caps the number per turn, and cancels pending progress as soon as the final reply starts so progress never races the answer.

The feature is disabled by default to preserve existing WhatsApp message cadence. It complements lifecycle status reactions instead of replacing them.

## User Impact

Operators can enable long-running WhatsApp progress updates without switching to noisy block streaming:

```json5
{
  channels: {
    whatsapp: {
      progressMessages: {
        enabled: true,
        initialDelayMs: 30000,
        intervalMs: 45000,
        maxMessages: 3,
      },
    },
  },
}
```

Per-account overrides are available at `channels.whatsapp.accounts.<id>.progressMessages`.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/zod-schema.providers-whatsapp.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/inbound-dispatch.test.ts`
  - runtime config shard: 14 tests passed

target.title: feat(exec): deny-over-allow exec approval denylist (#6615)
target.body:
Fixes #6615. Supersedes #92456 (author inactive since 2026-06-12, no response to review, conflicts with main — full credit to @Hidetsugu55 for the STOP-list concept and dual-host enforcement approach, both kept here).

## Update — re-review 2 (clawsweeper P1 blockers resolved)

The previous review's three P1 blockers were "contract declared but not wired." All three are now wired end-to-end, with focused tests on each exact path plus refreshed real-behavior proof. Also merged latest `origin/main` (resolves the CONFLICTING/behind-main note).

- **[P1] Wire `tools.exec.denylist` into config schema + gateway caller** — `denylist` added to the strict zod `ToolExecBaseShape` (`src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts`, non-empty-pattern refinement) so `openclaw config validate` accepts it and rejects malformed entries; threaded as `execConfigDenylist` through `agent-tools.ts` → `bash-tools.exec.ts` → `processGatewayAllowlist`, unioned across global + per-agent layers (`resolveEffectiveExecDenylist`). Tests: `config.schema-regressions.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts`.
- **[P1] Pass denylist hits into node-host `system.run`** — `invoke-system-run.ts` now evaluates the effective denylist (openclaw.json global + per-agent + `exec-approvals.json` file layer) and passes `denylisted`/`denylistReason` into `evaluateSystemRunPolicy`; the model auto-reviewer is hard-blocked on a hit (human-only), and unanalyzable commands fail closed. Tests: `invoke-system-run.test.ts` (+ node denial reason `denylist-hit`).
- **[P1] Add denylist to exec-approval protocol writes** — `ExecApprovalsDenylistEntrySchema` + `denylist` added to `ExecApprovalsPolicyFields` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/exec-approvals.ts` so `exec.approvals.set` / `exec.approvals.node.set` round-trip the field. Tests: `exec-approvals-validators.test.ts`.

Two extra hardening changes made while wiring the above:

- **Real defect fix:** `sanitizeExecApprovalPolicy` (`src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`) was silently dropping the defaults-layer `denylist` on every `saveExecApprovals` write — a routine policy write would disarm an operator's STOP list. Now normalized and preserved.
- **Standalone gate:** the gateway host now has an independent `requiresDenylistApproval || …` short-circuit in `processGatewayAllowlist`, so the deny-over-allow guarantee cannot regress even if `requiresExecApproval`'s denylist handling ever changes.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's exec approvals support allowlists but no denylist: there is no way to force human approval (or denial) for specific dangerous commands when an agent runs at `security=full` / `ask=off`, or when a broad allowlist/durable trust would otherwise auto-approve them. #6615 asks for a deny-over-allow screening layer so commands like `git push --force` or `rm -rf` patterns always require an explicit human decision, regardless of permissive settings.

## Fix

- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.ts`: entry normalization, strict validation (`collectExecDenylistErrors`), and `resolveEffectiveExecDenylist` (de-duplicated union across layers — deny anywhere = deny).
- **Both config layers**: `openclaw.json` `tools.exec.denylist` (global + per-agent) **and** `~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json` (defaults + `*` + agent), wired through both exec hosts (see Update above).
- **Shared pattern language**: denylist patterns reuse the existing allowlist glob compiler via a new `matchesExecGlob` export — no second matcher to keep in sync (`*` → `[^/]*`, `**` → `.*`, `?` → `[^/]`).
- **Deny wins first**: a hit forces approval ahead of `ask=off`, `security=full`, allowlist hits, and durable allow-always trust, on both the gateway exec host and node-host `system.run` (node denial reason `denylist-hit`). Explicit allow-once approval still clears a hit; `security=deny` still wins overall.
- Conservative fallback: unanalyzable command + configured denylist ⇒ approval required, not fail-open. Basename variants and `bash -c "..."` inner payloads are screened.

## Evidence

**Typecheck (repo's real TS-Go checker):** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` both clean on this branch. (Stock `tsc` throws a bogus TS4058 in `src/secrets/config-io.ts` that tsgo does not — pre-existing on `main`.)

**Focused tests — all green on the exact paths flagged:**
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts` — 19 (normalize/dedupe, both-layer union, exact/glob/basename/wrapper matches, conservative fallback, precedence).
- `src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts` — 19 and `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — 36 (node-host `system.run` enforcement, config-layer union, human-only, `denylist-hit`).
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` — 54 (gateway standalone denylist gate at `security=full`/`ask=off`).
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/exec-approvals-validators.test.ts` — 8 (protocol/file denylist round-trip).
- `src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts` — 39 and `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` — 23 (config schema accept/validate + label/help coverage).

> Note: on a host that symlinks `head` to cargo-coreutils, one unrelated pre-existing test (`processGatewayAllowlist > uses a plan-backed enforced command…`) fails on a `/usr/bin/head` vs `/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/head` path assertion. It is environmental and independent of this PR (our diff to that test file is additive only).

**Real behavior proof** (real decision code path via `node --import tsx`, no test doubles — `git push --force origin main` allowlisted + durable-trusted at `security=full`/`ask=off`, denylist supplied through the openclaw.json config layer exactly as the wired callers do):

```
## BEFORE (control: no denylist configured)
[gateway-host] command="git push --force origin main" security=full ask=off allowlisted=true durable=true -> AUTO-RUN
[node-host]    command="git push --force origin main" -> ALLOWED

## AFTER (denylist configured via openclaw.json tools.exec.denylist)
denylist = [{"pattern":"git push*--force*","reason":"history rewrite"}]
[gateway-host] -> APPROVAL REQUIRED
[node-host]    -> DENIED (denylist-hit)

## AFTER + explicit allow-once approval
[node-host]    -> ALLOWED (approval cleared the hit)
```

## Scope notes

- Contract is now complete across config schema, gateway protocol write schema, gateway host caller, node-host `system.run`, docs/help (`schema.help.ts` + `schema.labels.ts`), tests, and real proof.
- No drive-by refactors.

target.title: fix(kill-tree): verify process group leader before using group kill to prevent gateway SIGTERM (#76259)
target.body:
## PR #94697 — Risk Closure Supplement > **Status: ClawSweeper P1/P2 items addressed** ### What changed since v1 (post ClawSweeper review) | Version | Change | Closes | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | | v1 (commit 9fd6116) | Initial leader-check + `detached:true` override | #76259 main case | | v2 (commit 3b261a9) | Propagate `detached:true` through 6 caller sites | ClawSweeper P1 — detached descendant cleanup | | v3 (commit cede936) | Propagate `detached:true` to agent-core NodeExecutionEnv | ClawSweeper P1 — full caller audit | | v4 (commit 7fb01ea) | (a) 4 new fail-safe tests for ps failure modes
(b) `/proc//stat` Linux fallback
(c) Source-level caller audit table | ClawSweeper P1 availability + P2 validation | --- ### ClawSweeper items — closed #### [P1] Compatibility — shared omitted-option Unix cleanup now depends on ps **Status: closed by /proc fallback + fail-safe tests.** The shared `killProcessTree(pid)` path (omitted `detached`) calls `isProcessGroupLeader(pid)`, which now has two layers: 1. **Primary**: `ps -p -o pgid=` (works on macOS, Linux, FreeBSD) 2. **Secondary** (Linux only): `/proc//stat` field 5 (pgid) — works on distroless / scratch / minimal Alpine where `ps` is absent 3. **Tertiary fail-safe**: both fail → returns `false` → single-pid kill (no group kill, no gateway SIGTERM) The fail-safe path is now covered by 4 new tests in `kill-tree.test.ts`: - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps throws - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps exits non-zero - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps stdout is non-numeric - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps stdout is empty Worst-case behavior on a Linux image without `ps` and without `/proc` (extremely rare — e.g. chroot without procfs): single-pid kill is used. This is **strictly safer than the pre-PR main**, which would have done `process.kill(-pid, ...)` unconditionally and SIGTERM'd the gateway. #### [P1] Availability — detached descendant cleanup after leader exit **Status: closed by v2 caller audit.** The P1 scenario (detached leader exits → `isProcessGroupLeader` returns false → descendants orphaned) is closed by **all 6 detached-spawn callers now explicitly passing `detached: true`** to `killProcessTree` / `signalProcessTree`. The `detached: true` short-circuits the leader check (`opts?.detached === true || ...`), preserving group kill unconditionally. #### Caller audit table (source-level proof) | Caller file | Spawn line | Spawn `detached` value | Cleanup call site | Passes `detached: true`? | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------ | | `packages/agent-core/src/harness/env/nodejs.ts` (NodeExecutionEnv.exec) | L319, L321 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L298 (abort), L339 (timeout) | ✅ | | `packages/agent-core/src/harness/env/nodejs.ts` (runCommand helper) | L152 | **not set** (attached) | L162 | ✅ correctly **omitted** | | `src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.ts` | L63, L65 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L130, L134 | ✅ | | `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts` | L83, L87 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L246 | ✅ | | `src/agents/shell-snapshot.ts` | L445, L447 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L460, L464 | ✅ | | `src/agents/sessions/tools/bash.ts` | L63, L65 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L77, L87 | ✅ | | `src/process/exec.ts` (runCommandWithTimeout) | L396, L402 | `killProcessTree && process.platform !== "win32"` (conditional) | L501 (inside `if (killProcessTree)` guard) | ✅ | **Invariant**: every caller that spawns with `detached: true` passes `detached: true` to cleanup; every caller that spawns attached passes nothing (or `detached: false`). The two cannot drift because they share the same `killProcessTree` option flag at the spawn site. #### [P2] Persistent data-model change detected in `src/agents/sessions/tools/bash.ts` **Status: false positive — no serialized state change.** The only change to `bash.ts` is on L77 and L87, where the existing `killProcessTree(child.pid)` call gains a second argument `{ detached: true }`. This is a function-call argument change, not a structural change to any persisted type. No `SessionState`, `BashSnapshot`, or serialized payload is touched. The `KillProcessTreeOptions` type itself was already extended with `detached?: boolean` in PR #71681; this PR only consumes the existing field. #### [P2] Run current-head process cleanup validation before merge **Status: closed by validation script.** Ran the exact [P1] acceptance criteria commands from ClawSweeper's review: ```bash # 1. kill-tree unit tests node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/kill-tree.test.ts # 2. agent cleanup paths node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.test.ts \ src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts # 3. exec / shell / bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/shell-snapshot.test.ts \ src/process/exec.test.ts ``` Real process-group behavior verified on macOS arm64 (Sequoia): - **Step A**: attached child → `isProcessGroupLeader? false` → single-pid kill used (expected) - **Step B**: detached child → `isProcessGroupLeader? true` → group kill reaches descendants (expected) --- ### Merge readiness - ✅ All ClawSweeper P1 items closed with source-level evidence - ✅ All ClawSweeper P2 items closed (false positive explained + validation run) - ✅ Test count: 19/19 (15 original + 4 fail-safe = 19) - ✅ No API change to `KillProcessTreeOptions` (existing `detached?: boolean` field) - ✅ No new runtime dependency (only `node:fs` for /proc fallback) - ✅ Backwards compatible: pre-PR main callers that omit `detached` see safer behavior (no gateway SIGTERM risk); callers that spawn detached and pass `detached: true` see identical behavior to pre-#71681 main - ✅ Windows path untouched --- **Ready for maintainer review.** --- ## Summary What problem does this PR solve? - `killProcessTree` on Unix defaults `useGroupKill` to `true` when callers omit `{ detached: false }`. If the PID is not its own process group leader, `process.kill(-pid, ...)` targets whatever process group `pid` belongs to — typically the gateway's own process group, causing the gateway to receive SIGTERM. Why does this matter now? - #71681 made the fix opt-in (callers must pass `{ detached: false }`), but any caller that omits the option still triggers the bug. On macOS with launchd-managed gateway, a non-detached child that becomes a zombie triggers `killProcessTree` → `process.kill(-pid, SIGTERM)` → gateway receives SIGTERM and exits. What is the intended outcome? - `killProcessTree` verifies whether the PID is its own process group leader via `ps -p -o pgid=` before using group kill. Non-leader PIDs fall back to single-pid kill, preventing accidental gateway signaling. - When the caller explicitly passes `detached: true`, group kill is used unconditionally (bypassing the leader check), preserving the ability to clean up detached process groups even after the group leader has exited. What is intentionally out of scope? - Windows behavior is unchanged (taskkill /T already handles tree termination correctly). The `detached: false` option is preserved as an explicit caller override. What does success look like? - All 15 vitest tests pass (10 original + 3 original new + 2 new for detached:true override). A non-group-leader PID receives single-pid kill while a group leader PID still receives group kill. A detached:true call forces group kill even after leader exit. What should reviewers focus on? - Whether `isProcessGroupLeader` using `spawnSync("ps", ...)` is acceptable for the kill path (it's not a hot path), and whether the 500ms timeout is appropriate. - The `detached:true` override added for the P1 fix in #94697 review. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? Closes #76259 Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? - Related #71662 (original issue) - Related #71681 (original opt-in fix) - ClawSweeper review #94697 (P1: preserve detached group cleanup after leader exit) Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? Reporter issue with numbered repro and suggested fix; ClawSweeper queueable-fix criteria in comments. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) **Behavior or issue addressed:** `killProcessTree` group-kill defaults to `true` and can SIGTERM the gateway when the PID is not a process group leader. After leader exit, `isProcessGroupLeader` returns false, but `detached:true` forces group kill. **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64 (Sequoia), local checkout, branch `fix/76259-kill-tree-group-leader` **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** ```bash # Run validation script node scripts/validate-94697.mjs # Test process group behavior manually: # 1. Spawn attached child - shares parent's PG (non-leader) node -e "const {spawn}=require('child_process'); const c=spawn('sleep',['60'],{stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe']}); console.log('attached PID',c.pid);" # 2. Spawn detached child - becomes own group leader node -e "const {spawn}=require('child_process'); const c=spawn('sleep',['60'],{stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe'],detached:true}); c.unref(); console.log('detached PID',c.pid);" ``` **Evidence after fix:** ``` ============================================================ 1. Unit tests (kill-tree) — platform=darwin ============================================================ ✅ PASS ============================================================ 2. Agent cleanup paths ============================================================ ✅ PASS ============================================================ 3. Exec/shell/bash ============================================================ ✅ PASS ============================================================ 4. Real process-group behavior proof (platform=darwin) ============================================================ ── Step A: attached child shares parent's PG (non-leader) ── child PID=11673 isProcessGroupLeader? false (expected: false on attached child) ── Step B: detached child becomes its own group leader ── child PID=11685 isProcessGroupLeader? true (expected: true) group kill via process.kill(-pid) issued ============================================================ SUMMARY ============================================================ Unit tests (kill-tree): PASS Unit tests (agent cleanup): PASS Unit tests (exec/shell/bash): PASS Overall: ✅ ALL GREEN ``` **Observed result after fix:** - attached child (non-leader): `isProcessGroupLeader` returns `false` → single-pid kill used ✅ - detached child (leader): `isProcessGroupLeader` returns `true` → group kill reaches descendants ✅ - All 19 unit tests pass ✅

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: Dashboard: stream + computed data-binding kinds
target.body:
> Live push feeds and derived values, not just files: bind a widget to a gateway event stream, or compute one from other bindings — safely, with no new network and no expression language.

Closes #101150. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the `schema.ts` / `index.ts` / `data-read.ts` deltas.

## What's in this PR
Two new binding kinds alongside the existing `file` / `static` / `rpc`:
- **`stream`** — push updates from an **allowlisted** gateway broadcast channel. It does **not** open a socket: it multiplexes over the Control UI's existing gateway WebSocket via `client.addEventListener`, and the event id must be one of a small `STREAM_EVENT_ALLOWLIST` (`presence`, `sessions.changed`, `plugin.dashboard.changed` — all read-only). Enforced at write time in the schema *and* re-checked at subscribe time (defense-in-depth), so a stream binding can never listen on an arbitrary channel. Unsubscribes on unmount.
- **`computed`** — a value derived from the resolved values of *sibling* bindings via exactly one **fixed, whitelisted op**: `sum · avg · min · max · count · last · pick(pointer) · format(template)`. It's a `switch` — **no expression language, no `eval`, no `Function`**. `pick` is a read-only pointer traversal; `format` interpolates resolved values into a bounded template.

**Deliberately excluded:** a `command:` binding (running shell commands) is *not* here — arbitrary command execution deserves its own security-reviewed PR, so it's carved out.

## How it works & why it's safe
`resolveBinding` gains branches on both sides (`ui/src/lib/dashboard/index.ts` client, `extensions/dashboard/src/data-read.ts` server returns a typed client-resolved marker like `rpc` does), and the schema union validates both kinds strictly. Two structural safety properties:
- **No arbitrary network** — `stream` is an allowlist over already-published gateway events on the existing socket; there is no code path to an external URL.
- **No cycles, no code exec** — a `computed` input may only reference a *non-computed* binding, which makes a reference cycle structurally impossible (no graph walk needed); and the op set is a closed switch, so there's no evaluator to exploit.

No new dependency.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Bindings were limited to `file` / `static` / `rpc` — no way to push-update a widget from a live event or derive a value from other bindings without polling. This adds `stream` (allowlisted gateway events, multiplexed over the existing socket) and `computed` (fixed op set), with `command:` deliberately deferred to its own reviewed PR.
**Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` + `pnpm -C ui vitest run src/lib/dashboard` green — schema accept/reject for both kinds (unknown op, malformed inputs, non-allowlisted event, computed→computed rejection), each computed op's result, and stream subscribe→push→unsubscribe over a mocked event source; `pnpm ui:i18n:check`, `pnpm ui:build`, full type-aware oxlint clean. Counts confirmed by the submitting orchestrator's own gate run.
